status: Locally verified source extension after published 0.13.0. No new release, archives or production deployment. Full AgentOS parity remains open.

contract.get_foreground: (fd: u32, group_ptr: u32) -> WASI errno; writes a little-endian u32 group.
contract.set_foreground: (fd: u32, group: u32) -> WASI errno; accepts a live group in the caller session, including a stopped group.
contract.ownership: The existing native descriptor grants access to its terminal. Group lookup is confined to the current virtual process family. Caller/target session matching follows the inspected upstream kernel policy; controlling-terminal session acquisition is not implemented.

errors.63: Target group belongs to another session

contract.abiScope: These two host_tty imports are explicit Boxes extensions for compiled guest programs, not a claim that stock upstream WASI packages import them.

persistence: The existing shared native Terminal.foreground cell is the single owner. Aliases and master/slave ends see the same cell. The current native heap checkpoint retains the selected group and process table. No input-head shape, R2 namespace, data migration or infrastructure resource changes.

verification.nativeParent: A parent in group 1 gives its attached terminal to child group 2 through a duplicated descriptor. A separate-session group is rejected. Resize sends SIGWINCH to child 2; the parent trampoline would fail on a misrouted resize. Ctrl-Z stops the child, the parent observes WUNTRACED, changes foreground away and back while the child is stopped, sends SIGCONT and observes WCONTINUED. Ctrl-C exits the child with raw wait status 2. The exited group is rejected, group 1 reclaims foreground, and a later Ctrl-C reaches the parent handler. Three input bytes are retained exactly.
verification.nativePair: An internal PTY starts with foreground zero. Setting the slave to group 1 is visible through its master. Native master fd_write of Ctrl-C invokes the root handler once through the shared signal scheduler; the interrupted tty read completes and the guest exits zero.
verification.errorChecks: Invalid pointers, closed aliases, missing/invalid groups, non-terminal descriptors, cross-session selection and exited groups return their declared errno. Failed mutations retain the previous group.
verification.replacement: A real R2 checkpoint retains native handles 1 and 2, foreground 2, the parent wait frame and the child read with partial canonical input. After replacement, a later Ctrl-C targets child 2, clears the partial line once and allows the parent to reclaim group 1. Exact output, accepted offsets and complete replay survive duplicate Queue delivery without reentry.

initialFocusedRun.finding: Live parent/pair cases passed. Advancing the virtual clock on the first output during multi-child setup produced native Queue outcome exception and left the receipt running, before any checkpoint. Cause instrumentation did not expose a typed Effect failure.

steadyStateRecoveryProbe.change: Only the clock-advance readiness predicate changed for this probe: wait for the completed setup messages before advancing the same 30 seconds. No checkpoint/status/output assertion was removed and no timeout increased.

verification.clockHarness: Historical 2b7c35b probe used advanceAfterBytes to wait for completed setup. The deadline follow-up identified sleeps overshooting the absolute lease and removes this workaround, its bindings, Schema field and callers. Foreground now resumes with the clock advancing after the first output.

generalBenchmark.limits: Maintained local regression smoke only; no paired baseline or production performance claim. Existing performance evidence was preserved.

limits: The initial immediate-advance failure is resolved by the handover-deadline follow-up: relative sleeps could overshoot the 30-second lease. Its before/after native tests cover child wait, delayed poll and delayed stopped state. Broader arbitrary-interruption/admission coverage remains with the full recovery gates.
Controlling-terminal acquisition/session ownership, SIGTTIN/SIGTTOU background-access policy, raw-mode recovery leases, full termios and richer public terminal metadata/listing remain open.
Arbitrary-crash and cross-build native heap recovery remain open.
Remote CI and production delivery of this source increment are separate gates; no new performance or cost advantage is claimed.
